{{short description|French mathematician (born 1946)}}
[[File: Ledrappier.jpg | thumb|François Ledrappier, Oberwolfach 1976]]
'''François Ledrappier''' (born 17 January 1946) is a French mathematician.

Ledrappier graduated from the [[École Polytechnique]] in 1967 and received his doctorate from [[Pierre and Marie Curie University]] (Paris 6) in 1975 under the supervision of [[Jacques Neveu]].<ref name=MathGen>{{MathGenealogy|id=76858}}</ref> Ledrappier taught at Paris 6 and then became a professor at [[South Bend]]'s [[University of Notre Dame]], where he is now professor emeritus.

His research deals with asymptotic properties of [[Group action (mathematics)|group action]]s and related problems. He has published articles on [[dynamical system]]s theory, compact negatively curved manifolds and their abelian covers, linear actions and random walks on [[linear group]]s, [[geometric measure theory]], and zero entropy algebraic actions of [[free abelian group]]s.<ref>{{cite web|title=François Ledrappier|website=Department of Mathematics, University of Notre Dame|url=https://math.nd.edu/people/faculty/francois-ledrappier/}}</ref>

In 1994 Ledrappier was an invited speaker at the International Congress of Mathematicians in Zurich.<ref name="Ledrappier1995">{{cite book|last1=Ledrappier|first1=François|chapter=Applications of Dynamics to Compact Manifolds of Negative Curvature|title=Proceedings of the ICM (1994, Zürich)|year=1995|pages=1195–1202|doi=10.1007/978-3-0348-9078-6_113|isbn= 978-3-0348-9078-6}}</ref> In 2016 he received the [[Sophie Germain Prize]].<ref>[http://www.academie-sciences.fr/fr/Laureats/les-laureats-des-grands-prix-attribues-en-2016.html Lauréats des grands prix 2016].</ref>

His doctoral students include [[Nalini Anantharaman]].<ref name=MathGen/>
